compensating.why: hop 1 measures the weeks with a UK calendar
hop 2 measures the previous year at 28 December
hop 3 hands on the week number raised to at least the first week

context_edits.old:
/**
     * Returns the shape used for legend items.

edits.old: return year > 1900 ? new Week(lastWeek, year - 1) : null;

ownership_reason: Only the gold decides which week precedes the given week: the week numbered one less in the same year, or, for the first week, the last week of the year before. Hop 1 only supplies the calendar the weeks are measured with, hop 2 only measures the number of the last week of the previous year (for every week, the first week of 1900 included), and hops 3 and 4 pass the week, the year and that number along and return the week they are given. Once the gold has built the last week of 1899 for the first week of 1900, the null result can appear only if a caller answers that input itself instead of the gold or replaces the gold's week. The variant builds new Week(.., 1899), outside the documented domain of the Week(int, int) constructor ('the year (1900 to 9999)', the range of SerialDate.MINIMUM_YEAR_SUPPORTED to MAXIMUM_YEAR_SUPPORTED); the facade's javadoc states that the week before week 1 of 1900 is null. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact siblings Month.previous() and Quarter.previous() return null for the first period of 1900, Year.previous() returns null at SerialDate.MINIMUM_YEAR_SUPPORTED, and Week.next() applies the mirror limit (null after the last week of 9999); MonthTests::testJan1900Previous, QuarterTests::testQ1Y1900Previous and YearTests::test1900Previous pass, and WeekTests::testW52Y9999Previous passes through the chain.
